title: Integral cubical lattice chains retract onto the augmentation
statement:
For an integer $r\geq0$ put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, with standard basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. For $0\leq a\leq r$ let $C_a$ be the free abelian group [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on symbols $[v,I]$ with $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $a$, and put $C_a=0$ otherwise. Define
$$\partial_a[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}\bigl([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]\bigr),\qquad a\geq1.$$
Let $\epsilon:C_0\to\mathbf Z$ send every $[v,\varnothing]$ to $1$, let $s:\mathbf Z\to C_0$ send $1$ to $[0,\varnothing]$, and let $e:C_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ equal $s\epsilon$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Then $\partial_{a-1}\partial_a=0$, $\epsilon\partial_1=0$, and there are abelian-group homomorphisms $h_a:C_a\to C_{a+1}$ with
$$\partial_{a+1}h_a+h_{a-1}\partial_a=1-e_a\quad(a\geq0),\qquad \epsilon s=1,$$
where $h_{-1}\partial_0=0$. In particular $C_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathbf Z$ is exact as an augmented chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Translation $w[v,I]=[v+w,I]$ commutes with $\partial$ and $\epsilon$ (with trivial action on $\mathbf Z$); each $C_a$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the free integral $D$-module on $D$, one for each $I$ of size $a$. The maps $h_a$ and $s$ need not commute with translation. For $r=0$ take $s=\epsilon=1$ and $h=0$.

proof.text: Use the explicit constructions [def-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-chains]. Apply [lem-sfb-cubical-boundary-coordinate-projections] to the displayed groups and differential. It gives $\partial^2=0$, $\epsilon\partial_1=0$, the commuting coordinate chain maps $p_i$, and the product $P_r=e$, with $P_0=1$. Its basis-preserving decomposition also gives every translation and finite free-orbit assertion in the statement.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-cubical-signed-coordinate-homotopy] on exactly these basis groups and coordinate maps. Its finite signed-path formulas give homomorphisms $H_i$ in all degrees with $\partial H_i+H_i\partial=1-p_i$, including negative coordinate values and top degree. Set $h_a=\sum_{i=1}^r P_{i-1,a+1}H_{i,a}$. The sum is finite and $h_{-1}=0$. In Lean encode the finite sum recursively on List.finRange r: H_(i::L)=H_i+p_i H_L and H_empty=0.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: Each $P_i$ commutes with $\partial$ by [lem-sfb-cubical-boundary-coordinate-projections]. Using the identity supplied by [lem-sfb-cubical-signed-coordinate-homotopy] gives $$\partial h+h\partial=\sum_{i=1}^rP_{i-1}(1-p_i)=\sum_{i=1}^r(P_{i-1}-P_i)=1-P_r=1-e.$$ This is the required contraction in every nonnegative degree. Direct evaluation on $1$ gives $\epsilon s=1$. Equivalently, induct on the list: (1-p_i)+p_i(1-P_L)=1-p_i P_L. Degree transports commute with endomorphisms by equality induction.

proof.text: If $a>0$ and $\partial_a x=0$, this contraction gives $x=\partial_{a+1}h_a x$. If $a=0$ and $\epsilon x=0$, it gives $x=\partial_1h_0x$. Conversely every such boundary is in the corresponding kernel since $\partial^2=0$ and $\epsilon\partial_1=0$. Also $\epsilon$ is surjective since $\epsilon s=1$. Hence kernel equals image at every position of the augmented complex, precisely exactness in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: When $r=0$, [lem-sfb-cubical-boundary-coordinate-projections] identifies the singleton vertex basis with $\mathbf Z$, and both $s$ and $\epsilon$ become identities. The defining empty sum makes $h=0$. No equivariance of $h$ or $s$ is required; already for $r=1$, translation by $u_1$ sends $s(1)=[0,\varnothing]$ to $[u_1,\varnothing]$.
